sources.title: Suicide Food
sources.author: Ben (surname not given on the blog; named as Ben Grossblatt by The Stranger)
sources.note: 929 posts, 20 December 2006 to 27 December 2011, still online. Catalogued depictions of animals presented as wanting to be eaten and rated each on a five-point scale headed Psych Evaluations, counted in nooses. Post tags: pig 539, bbq 399, chicken 238, cow 210, chef hat 114, sunglasses 107. An eleven-part series from 2007 to 2011 named the recycled stock pig logo 'Repetitious Porcine Emblemology'. The last post calls itself an indefinite pause rather than a closure. Archived at the Wayback Machine from 14 June 2007.

sources.title: The Fiction Kitchen
Flickr Commons
sources.publisher: Flickr, with participating libraries, archives and museums
sources.note: Institutions publish photographs here under the rights statement 'No known copyright restrictions', which is not a public-domain declaration: the holding institution states it has found no copyright, shares that research without warranty, and asks the user to make an independent assessment before a new use. The statement is per photograph. The same institution's stream holds all-rights-reserved photographs alongside released ones, and the same negative sometimes appears both ways, so each file here was checked on its own page.

sources.title: State Archives of North Carolina on Flickr Commons
sources.publisher: State Archives of North Carolina, Raleigh
sources.note: Around 117,000 photographs from the State Archives' photograph collections. Uploads made from about 2015 onward generally carry 'No known copyright restrictions'; a body of 2008-era uploads of the same collections, and in places the same images, carries 'All rights reserved'. Photographs taken here were verified one page at a time; the refused ones are listed in data/harvest/picture-sources.json.

sources.title: Department of Conservation and Development, Travel Information Division Photograph Collection
sources.publisher: State Archives of North Carolina, Raleigh
sources.note: Photographs made by the state's own News Bureau for publicity use, many of them mounted on printed subject sheets with the locality and date written in by hand. John Hemmer and Bill Sharpe are the photographers named on the barbecue sheets. The sheets are the caption: the pencil on them is quoted in this project's alt text as writing on the object, not as a finding of fact.

sources.title: Albert Barden Collection, State Archives of North Carolina
sources.author: Albert Barden
sources.publisher: State Archives of North Carolina, Raleigh
sources.note: A Raleigh commercial photographer's negatives, roughly 1900 to the 1950s: shopfronts, filling stations, company dinners and one much-reproduced open-pit barbecue. Catalogue number N.53.17.314 appears in the stream three times — twice under 'No known copyright restrictions' and once, in an older upload, under 'All rights reserved' — and the two released scans are mirror images of each other, so the negative's orientation is not settled by this source.

sources.title: PhC.184 Massengill Postcard Collection
sources.publisher: State Archives of North Carolina, Raleigh
sources.note: North Carolina postcards, including linen-era and later chrome cards of named barbecue houses: Wilber's at Goldsboro, Parker's at Wilson, the Barbecue Lodge at Raleigh. Cards are undated in the collection's captions; the dates this project gives come from what is in the frame and are marked as such.

sources.title: H. H. Brimley Collection, PhC.42
sources.author: H. H. Brimley
sources.publisher: State Archives of North Carolina, Raleigh
sources.note: The photographs of Herbert Hutchinson Brimley, naturalist and first director of the North Carolina State Museum. The agriculture folders include free-ranging hogs on the Outer Banks around 1900 to 1905, captioned in the collection as scrub pigs and razorbacks.

sources.title: FCX Photograph Collection, PhC.23
sources.publisher: State Archives of North Carolina, Raleigh
sources.note: Photographs of the Farmers Cooperative Exchange, including Raleigh street views. The Clyde Cooper's Barbecue frame is captioned 1963 by the archive; the cars in it read later than that, so the date is carried as the archive's and not as this project's.
